The Baisaran War, also known as the Fifth Indo-Pakistani War, is an ongoing conflict between India and Pakistan that started in April 2025. The conflict started after India suspended the Indus Waters Treaty shortly after the Pahalgam Attack and provocations on the part of both sides. On 4 April, Pakistani and Indians forces on the Line of Control exchanged fire, escalating tensions further. Eventually, on XX MM 2025, war broke out between India and Pakistan for the first time in 25 years since the Kargil War.
Background
On 22 April 2025, 26 people were killed and dozens of others are injured when militant separatists open fire on tourists in Pahalgam, Indian-controlled Jammu and Kashmir. This attack was perpetrated by The Resistance Front, an offshoot of the UN-designated terrorist group Lashkar-e-Taiba. Following the attack, a joint cordon and search operation was launched by the Indian Army, paramilitary forces, and Jammu and Kashmir Police. A temporary lockdown was imposed in Pahalgam, and Indian Army helicopters were deployed to track down the militants, who reportedly fled to the upper reaches of the Pir Panjal range.
Escalation of Tensions
On 23 April, Indian foreign secretary Vikram Misri held a press conference announcing the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty on the part of the Indian government, suspension of all visas held by Pakistanis and a travel ban. This caused the Pakistani government to state that any action involving water could be considered an "act of war." On 24 April, Pakistan retaliated to the Indian government's actions by also suspending visas held by Indians, closed airspace to India, expelled diplomats and instructed Indian military officials to leave the country by 30 April, alongside suspending the Simla Agreement. Trade has ceased.
On 25 April, Indian military personnel deployed to the Line of Control as part of a joint cordon and search operation exchanged fire with Pakistani military personnel. No casualties were reported however according to the Indian government.
